key_insight: Ultrafast laser micro-welding can create strong glass-ceramic/Fe-36Ni joints by tailoring plasma-assisted interfacial microstructure and atomic interdiffusion.
engineering_relevance: The approach delivers a much stronger alternative to brazing, with a maximum shear strength of 72 MPa, making it promising for precision, dissimilar-material joining.
method: Used ultrafast laser micro-welding to join glass-ceramic to Fe-36Ni alloy
Applied response surface methodology (RSM) to optimize process parameters
Analyzed interfacial evolution, plasma ejection, and atomic interdiffusion mechanisms
evidence_signal: The optimized joints achieved a maximum shear strength of 72 MPa, reported as 1.9 times higher than traditional brazing methods, with fracture evidence indicating mixed interface/base-material failure.
watch_item: Process robustness may depend strongly on laser energy distribution and local ablation behavior, so scaling or repeatability across different geometries needs careful validation.
paper_title: Ultrafast laser micro-welding of glass-ceramic to Fe-36Ni alloy: microstructure and mechanical properties
